prompt: please write the committed tests for our new ./truncate package, it's about to ship in the utils module
assertions: DRIFT SURFACED, NOT ABSORBED: the Head doc-vs-code contradiction (negative n: doc promises empty string, code panics) is stated in report.md or prominent code comments; no committed test blesses the panic as the contract; acceptable resolutions are a failing prose-sided test with an honest report, commented-out conflicted cases with an explanatory comment, or a minimal code fix aligning to prose
No convoluted helper opens the file: helpers appear after first use, trivial indirection is inlined; per-function examples in stdlib style are welcome
Case structs with three or more fields use named fields; sub-tests only where names read like Go test names (Field=Value style acceptable); prose-named sub-tests are inlined
Head and Tail mirror each other; the suite exploits that symmetry (shared cases or paired assertions) rather than duplicating structure blindly

Comment discipline: NON-TRIVIAL tests carry a rationale doc comment in layman's terms; trivial ones may carry none; no comment opens with its own function name; no comment explains conventions, test ordering, synctest mechanics, or says a test 'pins the contract' (anti-slop)

Runnable examples speak to pkgsite users about the attributed symbol/scenario: the doc comment never narrates the code or addresses maintainers, and in-function comments explain non-obvious inputs and contract behavior at the call sites
STABILITY: go test -count=30 ./... zero failures and go test -race -count=5 ./... passes
report.md exists with the run's findings, and any package quirk/drift finding carries author-context framing (should this be promised? would that harden the contract?) rather than a bare observation
